blindSummary:
In August 2025, a 25-year-old newly crowned winner of an LGBTQ pageant held in a district of a nearby city was found with 13 stab wounds in this state/province. Police opened a homicide case within days of the crowning — a faster institutional response than the unresolved shooting of an activist in a neighbouring state/province — but the incident still represents one of the six national killings and occurred in a unit with no protective ordinance cluster.

Net effect: a moderate negative deviation from the national baseline. The single-incident rule applies: one killing in eighteen months is not a patterned violence trend for this unit, but the stabbing with 13 wounds and the LGBTQ-pageant context mark it as trans-implicated. The positive element (rapid homicide investigation) prevents a deeper deviation. Compare another state/province whose single killing involved alleged kidnapping and rape — slightly more prolonged violence but also a three-suspect identification within weeks; this unit edges slightly below its neighbour on the severity of the 13-wound attack.
